title: A three-frame story with continuity
goal: Translate a short narrative into consistent visual briefs and inspect change across frames.
explanation: Separate the story’s changing action from its fixed character and setting details. Repeating a style phrase does not guarantee continuity; reference-image support and controls vary by tool. Use an original fictional character, no real likeness, and keep all three frames as separate artifacts with a continuity ledger.
sampleInput: Original story: A small orange maintenance robot finds a seed on a rooftop. It plants the seed in a cracked blue pot. At sunrise it shelters the first leaf from the wind. Fixed details: round body, one square eye, blue pot, same rooftop; no logos or writing.
prompt: Create three separate frame briefs, one per sentence. For each list fixed character/prop details, action, camera view and light. Use one coherent hand-drawn editorial style. Do not change the robot’s eye, pot colour or rooftop between frames. Do not claim that prompt repetition guarantees visual consistency.
workedExample: Continuity ledger: robot round/orange/one square eye in all frames; pot blue once introduced; same rooftop edges. The action and time/light may change. A second eye or red pot is a continuity error, not a new story fact.

steps.title: Write the three sentences
steps.text: Keep the plot simple enough to show one action per frame.

steps.title: Make a continuity sheet
steps.text: Separate permanent character/setting features from allowed changes.

steps.title: Draft three briefs
steps.text: Require fixed details in each brief; avoid copying a known fictional franchise.

steps.title: Generate or draw separately
steps.text: Use a permitted reference workflow if available; otherwise record the lack of identity controls.

steps.title: Review as a sequence
steps.text: Compare all fixed features and note at least one correction before presenting the story.

checks: There are three separately described frames with one clear action each.
Fixed robot, prop and setting details are checked across the sequence.
The report documents continuity failures and actual controls used rather than promising perfect consistency.
commonMistakes: Treating style consistency as character consistency.
Using a real person’s likeness or a recognizable character without permission.
offline: Draw three thumbnail frames from the continuity sheet and have a reader reconstruct the story.
reflection: Which small visual inconsistency changed the story’s meaning?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. There are three separately described frames with one clear action each.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Fixed robot, prop and setting details are checked across the sequence.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Treating style consistency as character consistency.
